Date. 3 - 1 - 30.
Shanghai, 31st December, 1929.

The Director of Criminal Investigation,
Shanghai Municipal Police,
SHANGHAI.

Dear Sir,

With reference to our representative's call upon you
recently in connection with the trouble as had aboard our s.s.
"Luenho" in respect of Tea-boys and their respective Union and
Society, we beg to enclose herewith copy of a letter dated 30th
instant addressed to us by The Chinese Seamen's Union, which we pass
on for your information and files. We would advise that we do not
propose taking any action as suggested by them.

We wish to take this opportunity of thanking you for the
ready response to our request for Police assistance, and for your
detailing Inspector Prince and other officers to attend the examination
of passes on board our s.s. "Luenho" on the evening of the 19th inst.
and for protection in case it became necessary, all of which was, we
assure you, greatly appreciated.

With best wishes.

We are, Dear Sir,
Yours faithfully,
Per pro. JARDINE, MATHESON & Co., Ltd.

General Managers, Indo-China S. N. Co., Ltd.

敬启者：

关于我方代表近日就本公司“联和”号（Luenho）轮上茶房及其各自工会和社团引发的纠纷一事拜访 阁下，现随函附上中国海员工会于本月30日致我方信函副本一份，供 贵方参考存档。我们要告知的是，对于该工会建议采取的行动，我方不拟采纳。

借此机会，我们要感谢 贵方对我方请求警方协助的快速响应，并感谢 贵方指派普林斯（Prince）巡官及其他警官于本月19日晚登临本公司“联和”号轮查验通行证，以及在必要时提供保护。我们可以向 贵方保证，对此我们深表感激。

顺颂时祺。

此致
敬礼，
谨代表 怡和洋行有限公司

30th December, 1929.

The Shipping Manager,
Jardine, Matheson & Co.,
The Bund, Local.

Dear Sir:

I had come to see you on last Saturday morning concerning
the excessive number of tea-boys of s.s. Luen Ho, but I was denied
from having this privilege owing to your being busily engaged to
other important matters.

In accordance with what we have previously settled those
teaboys without "passes" should leave the said ship on the last
sail. And according to the report we received, those old teaboys,
who are the members of the Union, did leave the ship through our
instruction, but the new teaboys who are employed by the money
shroff, went back again just before the ship started sailing.
Evidently the compradores of the said ship must be responsible for
this and its future unfortunate outcome.

We now request you to take adequate action towards this
matter immediately as a necessary step in avoiding unexpected
trouble and hope you will favour us with a reply at your earliest
convenience.

Yours very sincerely,

(Sgd.) So-ming Chiu, Secretary.

1929年12月30日。

航运经理，
怡和洋行，
外滩，本地。

敬启者：

上周六上午我曾前来拜会 阁下，商谈“联和”号轮茶房人数过多之事，但因 阁下忙于其他重要事务，未能获准面谈。

根据我们此前达成的协议，那些没有“通行证”的茶房应在最后一次航行中离开该船。据我们收到的报告，那些身为工会会员的老茶房已遵照我们的指示离船，但由银房雇员雇佣的新茶房在船只即将开航前又回到了船上。显然，该船的买办必须对此及其未来可能产生的不良后果负责。

我们现在请求 阁下立即就此事项采取适当行动，作为避免意外纠纷的必要步骤，并希望 阁下能在方便时尽早赐复。

此致
最诚挚的问候，

（签名）邱少明，秘书。

Indo-China S. N. Co., Ltd..
Re' Compradore's Staff on S.S. Luen Wo.

Sir,
Reference to the attached, and in accordance with instructions, I visited the Indo-China S.N. Co. Ltd. Office where I interviewed (on Dec.19 a.m.) Mr. Jacobs, and the Manager of the Department Mr. Aucott, regarding trouble among the Compradore's Staff, Waiters &c, on the s.s. Luen Wo (联和). Mr. Aucott informed me that they were having some trouble over the extraordinary number of "waiters" "Tea Boys" on the s.s. Luen Wo (联和), and that he had been approached by one Chui Sze Ming (徐士明), who styled himself "Secretary of the Chinese Seamen's Union Reorganisation Bureau", the offices of which are situated at No.450 Jukong Road, Chapei. This man proposed to go on board the s.s. Luen Wo to settle the trouble among the staff but Mr. Aucott politely and emphatically informed him that his company did not recognise any union, and that his services were not required on the ship. Mr. Aucott informed me that this man's manner was somewhat aggressive, and he expressed, in veiled threats possibility of further trouble on the ship. This was evidently an attempt to enforce recognition of the Seamen's Union to which this man belongs and accept his assistance in settling the trouble on the ship. Mr. Aucott further informed me that the registered number of "Waiters" "Tea-Boys" on the ship was 61, and these men have "Passes" bearing their name, photograph, and signature of the Company's Marine Superintendent, Mr. Rolfe, but it was found that altogether there were 137 men who claimed to be "waiters" on the ship, shewing an excess of 76 above the authorised number. The authorised ^waiters^T "Tea Boys" although recognised by the Company as the Compradore's Staff

印度支那轮船有限公司..
关于“联和”号轮买办职员事宜。

先生，
参照附件，并根据指示，我走访了印度支那轮船有限公司办公室，并于12月19日上午会见了雅各布斯（Jacobs）先生及部门经理奥科特（Aucott）先生，商讨“联和”号轮（联和）上买办职员、侍者等人员之间的纠纷。奥科特先生告诉我，他们在“联和”号轮（联和）上“侍者”、“茶房”人数异常过多的问题上遇到了一些麻烦，并且有一个名叫徐士明（Chui Sze Ming）的人找过他，此人自称是“中国海员工会改组局”秘书，该局办公室位于闸北巨鹿路450号。此人提议登上“联和”号轮以解决职员间的纠纷，但奥科特先生礼貌而坚决地告知他，公司不承认任何工会，且不需要他在船上提供服务。奥科特先生告诉我，此人的态度 somewhat aggressive（略显咄咄逼人），并以隐晦的威胁表达了船上可能发生进一步纠纷的可能性。这显然是试图强迫公司承认此人所属的海员工会，并接受其协助来解决船上的纠纷。奥科特先生还告诉我，船上注册的“侍者”、“茶房”人数为61人，这些人持有印有姓名、照片以及公司海事总监罗尔夫（Rolfe）先生签名的“通行证”，但发现共有137人声称是船上的“侍者”，显示出超出授权人数76人。经授权的^侍者^T “茶房”虽然被公司承认为买办职员

are not paid by either the company or Compradore, in fact,
it is stated, they pay for the previlege of being on the
staff by depositing $100$ or $150$ with the Compradore or
money shroff.
Of the 61 registered "Waiters" on the ship
38 belong to the Seamens' Union in Jukong Road, 6 belong to
a branch of this union in the City,and the remaining 17
belong to the Seamens' Guild, No.901 East Hanbury Road.
Now it appears that difficulties have arisen
over the Customs Authorities complaining about the excessive
number of these unpaid "Waiters", on the ship, who evidently
exist by smuggling and other illegitimate means, and those
unauthorised waiters on the ship who mostly belong to the
Seamen's Union in Jukong Road, have tried, with the assistance
of their union, to oust the authorised "Waiters", who are not
members of their union, so that they can possibly get their
places. It seems evident also that the Compradore- has been
influenced in this direction as he suggested dismissing the
whole of the staff of "Waiters" and engaging a new lot,who
would no doubt all be members of the Jukong Road Union, but
Mr.Aucott did not approve of this as he did not see why men
with many years of faithful service should be thrown out to
please any union or its officials.
On Dec. 9, a "notice" regarding the presence of
unauthorised "Tea-Boys" was drawn up and and posted in the
s.s. Luen Wo to let these men know the wishes of the Company
in respect of the Customs Authorities, and the Company's attitude
towards unauthorised persons on board their ships. "Copy of
this notice is attached".
At 5 p.m. Dec.19, D.I. Koo and I accompanied
Messrs Aucott and Jacobs on board the s.s. Luen Wo where we
shroffed the Passes of the 61 authorised "Waiters" on the ship

但实际上并非由公司或买办支付薪水，据说，他们是通过向买办或银房存入100或150美元来获得在职员名单上的特权。
在船上61名注册的“侍者”中，38人属于巨鹿路的海员工会，6人属于该市的一个分会，其余17人属于汉密尔顿路901号的海员公会。
目前看来，困难源于海关当局抱怨船上这些无薪“侍者”人数过多，这些人显然依靠走私和其他非法手段生存，而船上那些未经授权的大多属于巨鹿路海员工会的侍者，在工会的协助下，试图排挤不属于该工会的经授权“侍者”，以便他们可能获得这些职位。同样明显的是，买办也受到了这方面的影响，因为他建议解雇全体“侍者”职员，并雇佣一批新人，这些人无疑都将是巨鹿路工会的成员，但奥科特先生不赞成这样做，因为他不明白为什么要为了取悦某个工会或其官员而抛弃那些服务多年、忠诚可靠的员工。
12月9日，起草了一份关于存在未经授权“茶房”的“通知”，并张贴在“联和”号轮上，让这些人了解公司 regarding the Customs Authorities（关于海关当局）的意愿，以及公司对船上未经授权人员的态度。“该通知副本附后”。
12月19日下午5时，古（Koo）副督察和我陪同奥科特先生和雅各布斯先生登上“联和”号轮，在那里我们查验了船上61名经授权“侍者”的通行证

- TEA BOYS -

The Customs Authorities have recently complained about smuggled goods, and the large quantities of "pidgin" cargo carried on the Company's vessels, and request that prompt steps be taken to stop this nuisance, otherwise serious trouble will arise. They complain that a lot of this trouble is due to the excessive number of tea boys carried.

The Customs Authorities are aware that the Company allows a specified number of Tea Boys on each ship who are provided with passes signed by the Company's Marine Superintendent.

The Shipping Manager has recently travelled up river and has discovered that there are numbers of Tea Boys on board our vessels greatly in excess of the number allowed by the Company.

In order that the wishes of the Customs Authorities may be carried out, and serious trouble avoided, the Company now issues a warning that only such tea boys as have passes in their possession, signed by the Company's Marine Superintendent will be recognised, and any others must either leave the ship, or pay for their passages.

JARDINE, MATHESON & CO., LTD.,
General Managers,
Indo-China Steam Navigation Co., Ltd.
Shanghai, 9th December 1929.

- 茶房 -

海关当局最近投诉走私货物，以及公司船只上携带的大量“私货”（pidgin cargo），并要求迅速采取措施制止这种滋扰，否则将发生严重纠纷。他们抱怨许多此类麻烦是由于船上茶房人数过多所致。

海关当局知晓，公司允许每艘船上有一定数量的茶房，并由公司海事总监签发通行证。

航运经理最近溯江而上，发现我们船只上的茶房人数大大超过了公司允许的数量。

为了贯彻海关当局的意愿，并避免严重纠纷，公司现发出警告，只有持有公司海事总监签发的通行证的茶房才会被认可，其他任何人必须要么离船，要么支付船费。

怡和洋行有限公司，
总经理，
印度支那轮船有限公司。
上海，1929年12月9日。
